chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A man does not buy silver for gold unless it is hand-to-hand, and he does not buy gold for silver unless it is hand-to-hand.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for exchanging gold for silver in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith links the Prophet’s practice to Imam al-Sadiq and ultimately Imam Ali, establishing the 'hand-to-hand' (qabd) rule for gold and silver as *ribawi* items to prevent *riba al-fadl*. This immediate exchange ensures parity in weight and quality, serving as a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between simple currency exchange and interest-based usury.
